No front door

Followers stay followers

A woman can save your posts for a year and never join an email list. Every day without a class capturing emails is attention you earned and don't get to keep.

Free calls

Your calendar does the filtering

When the first step is a free call, anyone can book it. You spend coaching hours on women who were curious, not ready, and the ready ones wait in line behind them.

Content treadmill

267 posts and counting

Growth still leans on the next post. When you take a week off to rest, the enquiries take a week off too.

The women who love your content but aren't ready for 12 weeks today have no small, clear next step, so most of them take none.

My recommendation

A $17 masterclass that pays for its own ads and fills your 12 week program

You already have the audience and the signature program. What's missing is one paid 60-minute class that teaches your ancestral approach, offers a starter kit on the thank-you page, and invites the right women to apply for the 12 week program. Meta ads then put that class in front of new women every day.

Fixes the missing front door

A $17 seat is an easy yes for a woman who loves your content. Every buyer is an email you own and a customer who has already paid you once.

Replaces the free call

The replay page invites women who want your full support to apply. You only talk to people who paid, watched, stayed and told you where they are, so your calls are with buyers.

Pays for the ads

Seat sales and the starter kit bring money in on the front end, so the ad spend is largely covered before a single 12 week client signs.

The 95%*

Not ready for 12 weeks yet

They buy a $17 seat, many add the starter kit, and they keep learning from your emails and content. Your $260 offer stays there as a middle step for when they want more.

The qualified 5%

Ready for your full support

They watch to the end and apply on the replay page. The application filters for fit before your calendar, and three pre-call emails warm them up for the 12 week program.

*The 95% / 5% split is an industry estimate, not your data.
